A.explanation: Particles in the same loop between two adjacent nodes all move up and down together, so they are in phase with each other.

B.explanation: At an antinode the two creating waves reinforce, so the maximum amplitude is $2A$, twice the amplitude $A$ of each progressive wave.

C.explanation: The separation of two adjacent nodes is half a wavelength, $\lambda/2$, not the full wavelength $\lambda$.

D.explanation: It is a node that has zero displacement at all times, while an antinode oscillates with maximum amplitude.

hints: Look at the words node and antinode in the options - a node always has zero displacement and an antinode has maximum displacement.
Recall how phase works in a loop: all points between the same two adjacent nodes reach maximum displacement at the same time, but points on opposite sides of a node move oppositely.
Check the standard distances and amplitudes: adjacent node to node is $\lambda/2$ and the antinode amplitude is built from two waves of amplitude $A$ superposing.
walkthrough: Picture a stationary wave as two identical progressive waves travelling in opposite directions superposing. Nodes are fixed points of destructive interference with zero displacement, antinodes are points of maximum oscillation midway between nodes.
Between two adjacent nodes is one loop. All particles in that loop move in the same direction at the same time and pass through equilibrium together, so their phase difference is zero.
Across a node the motion reverses, so the next loop is in antiphase, but within one loop the in-phase rule holds.

Test the other quantities. The antinode amplitude is the sum of the two wave amplitudes, $A + A = 2A$, not $A$. The distance from one node to the next node is only $\lambda/2$, so a full wavelength $\lambda$ needs two loops.
Also, zero displacement at all times describes a node, not an antinode, which oscillates with the largest displacement.
Therefore only the statement about all particles between two adjacent nodes oscillating in phase is correct. This is option A
